# Low-seat contact repair status

New user authorization follows the completed low_positive_transfer_01 study. This is a separate experiment; previous results and policies remain unchanged.

Prepared low_seat_contact_01, verified 24,242 protected files, reserved 24 fresh holdout trials, and recorded all 60 previously successful conditions across the three now-development banks. Twelve cases remain unresolved across every current policy. No new training or fresh holdout evaluation has started.

Recorded diagnosis found about 0.6 mm predicted housing clearance on the 36 cm/+20 degree endpoint. Near the main low-seat failures, the pelvis is approximately 6–10 mm below and 7–21 mm farther inward than the planned root trajectory. Fresh geometry is available. These observations motivate damping and clearance experiments; they do not prove a sole cause.

The first two 24-case matched comparisons are complete and rejected. Both baselines had 22/24 stable, 8/24 clean, 16 slipping and two housing-contact cases on this deliberately difficult probe bank. Damping alone retained those outcomes without fixing the failures. The forward-clearance candidate lost 12 stable cases and added eight physical-failure cases (10/24 stable, 8/24 clean, 10 contacts/physical failures). Exact startups and first ten seconds passed independent audits. Bound/finger checks passed; estimator errors reached 3.5 mm in the damping probe and 11.8 mm in the failed clearance probe. All 24,242 prior hashes were independently rechecked intact.

The two load-feedback probes also completed and are rejected. load_feedback_original_02: 18 stable, 8 clean, 16 slipping, two contacts/physical failures; four stable cases lost. load_feedback_clearance_02: 10 stable, 8 clean, 16 slipping, eight unwanted-contact cases and 12 physical failures; ten added physical-failure cases. Their independent outcome and sensor/controller audits are saved. No physical criteria were relaxed. All four failed candidates and their matched baseline evidence are protected in rejected_probes_preservation_02.json.

The normal-descent pair completed at 02:55 UTC. normal_descent_03: 20 stable, 12 clean, ten slipping and two housing-contact/physical-failure cases. It gained four clean cases (37 cm/+11.25° and 36.5 cm/+12.5°, two placements each) but lost stable support on 40 cm/+20°. hover_rotate_normal_03: ten stable, eight clean, 16 slipping and ten contacts/physical failures; rejected. Both exact-startup/prefix audits and sensor-control checks passed as software audits, not admission. normal_diagnosis_03.json correctly maps geometry through each episode's geometry_index. The 36 cm/+20° candidate moved about 60 mm farther inward than its planned root path and contacted a housing before the pelvis took weight. Normal descent is promising on some cases, not a complete repair.

The balance-handoff probes completed at 03:22 UTC and are rejected: normal_ankle_balance_04 had 14 stable, 12 clean, ten slipping and four contacts/physical failures; normal_load_balance_04 had 16 stable, 12 clean, ten slipping and four contacts/physical failures. Both added housing-contact cases at 36.5 cm/+17.5°. Changing the timed balance handoff alone did not fix the problem. Exact startups/first10s, fixed fingers, and independent balance fraction/estimated-load replay passed. The first new offline audit incorrectly expected the plan to be consumed in the same tick it was installed; original source/failure is preserved in balance_audit_recovery_01, and v2 uses the next callback with unchanged numerical tolerances.
